newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss June inflation slows to 0.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Swiss June inflation slows to 0.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Swiss consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in June from May for a year-on-year inflation rate of 0.5 percent, the Federal Statistics Office said.
Monthly CPI index change +0.1 pct -0.3 pct +0.1 pct
The office said the monthly rise was mainly attributable to an 0.6 percent increase in prices for food, beverages and tobacco, reflecting seasonal price rises.

The categories for transport and communications as well as home furnishings both went up 0.2 percent, while prices for entertainment, leisure, education and culture dipped 0.2 percent. Rents and energy slipped 0.1 percent. Other categories were steady.
Prices of domestic products were stable, while imports rose 0.3 percent. Compared with June 1996, domestic goods prices rose an average 0.5 percent and those of imports went up 0.6 percent.
The biggest price changes compared with June 1996 were rises of 0.9 percent for health care and 0.8 percent for rents and energy.
